title: PVSync: A Unified Lip-Sync Expert for Timing and Articulation
title_zh: PVSync：一种统一的唇部同步专家模型，用于时序与发音协调

paragraphs.en: Lip movements can match the timing of speech without matching the spoken sounds. We introduce PVSync, a unified model for audio–visual offset estimation and phoneme-level articulation scoring. PVSync combines window-level contrastive learning for synchronisation with a phoneme-level articulation objective that aligns audio and video embeddings of the same viseme class across clips. Visemes group phonemes with similar visible articulation. Viseme labels are derived automatically from forced-aligned transcripts, without manual annotations. On videos from 13 13 talking-head video generation models, PVSync matches human rankings of lip-sync quality more closely than LSE-C, achieving a Spearman correlation of 0.83 0.83 versus 0.34 0.34 . On an automatically constructed benchmark from held-out speech, PVSync distinguishes viseme-matched from mismatched audio–visual pairs with an ROC AUC of 0.91 0.91 . PVSync also recovers the offset within one frame on 92.7 true % 92.7\text{true}\mathrm{\%} of held-out in-the-wild clips, against 87.4 true % 87.4\text{true}\mathrm{\%} for MTD-VocaLiST and 80.0 true % 80.0\text{true}\mathrm{\%} for SyncNet. Code and benchmark data will be released upon acceptance.
paragraphs.zh: 嘴唇动作可以与语音的时机同步，但未必与发出的声音一致。 我们提出了 PVSync，一个用于音频-视觉偏移估计和音素级发音评分的统一模型。 PVSync 将窗口级对比学习用于同步，并结合了音素级发音目标，使同一视素类别的音频和视频嵌入在不同片段中保持一致。 视素将具有相似可见发音特征的音素归为一类。 视素标签通过强制对齐的转录文本自动推导，无需人工标注。 在来自 13 个说话头部视频生成模型的视频上，PVSync 对唇部同步质量的人类排名匹配度高于 LSE-C，Spearman 相关系数达到 0.83（对比 0.34）。 在一个从预留语音数据中自动构建的基准数据集上，PVSync 通过 ROC AUC 值 0.91 区分了视素匹配的音频-视觉对与不匹配的对。 PVSync 还在 92.7% 的预留真实场景片段中实现了单帧内的偏移恢复，优于 MTD-VocaLiST 的 87.4% 和 SyncNet 的 80.0%。 代码和基准数据将在论文被接受后发布。

paragraphs.en: Accurate lip-sync requires more than temporal alignment. A generated mouth can move in time with speech yet fail to close for /p/ or form the lip–tooth contact required for /f/. Clip-level scores may obscure these brief errors, motivating evaluation of both timing and local articulation.
paragraphs.zh: 准确的唇形同步不仅需要时间上的对齐。 生成的嘴巴虽然能随着语音同步移动，却可能无法在发 /p/ 音时闭合，或无法形成发 /f/ 音所需的唇齿接触。 片段级别的评分可能会掩盖这些短暂错误，因此有必要同时评估时间同步和局部发音的准确性。

paragraphs.en: We introduce PVSync , a unified model for temporal offset estimation and phoneme-level articulation scoring in a shared audio–visual embedding. A contrastive objective aligns same-viseme audio and video spans across clips, alongside window-level synchronisation learning. Labels come from forced-aligned transcripts, without manual annotation. A final projection-head fine-tuning stage improves temporal precision while retaining articulation-sensitive representations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 PVSync，这是一种统一模型，用于在共享的音视频嵌入中估计时间偏移并打分音素级的发音。 一种对比目标将不同片段中相同视素对应的音频和视频片段对齐，同时结合窗口级的同步学习。 标签来自强制对齐的转录文本，无需人工标注。 最后的投影头微调阶段可在保留对发音敏感的表示的同时，提升时间精度。

paragraphs.en: VocaLiST [ 4 ] , MTD-VocaLiST [ 5 ] , Synchformer [ 6 ] and SyncLipMAE [ 7 ] focus on offset estimation. Jawade et al. [ 8 ] address dubbed-video content mismatch through ranking-based training, but produce a clip-level score. PhoVis [ 9 ] and FluentLip’s phoneme error rate [ 10 ] score phoneme-level errors with landmark templates and an AV-HuBERT lip-reader, but both compare the mouth with transcribed phoneme labels, not the audio itself, and neither estimates an offset. PVSync unifies learned cross-modal phoneme-level scoring and offset estimation.
paragraphs.zh: VocaLiST [ 4 ]、MTD-VocaLiST [ 5 ]、Synchformer [ 6 ] 和 SyncLipMAE [ 7 ] 专注于偏移量估计。Jawade 等人 [ 8 ] 通过基于排名的训练解决了配音视频中内容不匹配的问题，但仅能生成片段级别的分数。 PhoVis [ 9 ] 和 FluentLip 的音素错误率 [ 10 ] 利用地标模板和 AV-HuBERT 唇部识别模型对音素级别的错误进行评分，但两者都将嘴巴与转录后的音素标签进行比较，而非音频本身，且均未估计偏移量。 PVSync 将学习到的跨模态音素级别评分与偏移量估计统一了起来。

The video tower is AV-HuBERT Base [ 11 ] video-only, reading 88 × 88 88\times 88 grayscale mouth ROIs; the audio tower is wav2vec2-base [ 12 ] read at layer 8 over the matching 7680 7680 samples. The video tower emits one 768 768 -d token per frame and the audio tower one every 20 true ms 20\text{true}\mathrm{ms} , so a window gives 12 12 video tokens and 23 23 audio tokens, 𝐇 v ∈ ℝ 12 × 768 \mathbf{H}^{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{12\times 768} and 𝐇 a ∈ ℝ 23 × 768 \mathbf{H}^{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{23\times 768} ( Fig. 2 ). The audio count is 23 23 rather than 24 24 because the front end has a 400 400 -sample receptive field at a 320 320 -sample stride and no padding, so ⌊ ( 7680 − 400 ) / 320 ⌋ + 1 \lfloor(7680-400)/320\rfloor+1 tokens fit and the last partial stride is dropped. paragraphs.en: Protocol. We follow VocaLiST’s evaluation protocol [ 4 ] . Each test clip’s audio is aligned to its SyncNet-detected offset ( Section 3.1 ), so the true offset is zero. Each model judges a fixed-length input, 12 12 frames for PVSync. To decide over a longer context of K K frames, we shift the audio by a candidate offset, score every input-length window inside those K K frames one frame apart, and average the scores. Over the candidate offsets from − 15 -15 to + 15 +15 frames, the predicted offset is the one with the highest average, and it is correct within one frame of zero. The SyncNet row is therefore a self-consistency baseline. The test set is 3698 3698 held-out clips from Hallo3, CelebV-Text, CelebV-HQ, VFHQ and RAVDESS. Baselines are SyncNet [ 1 ] , MTD-VocaLiST [ 5 ] (standing in for VocaLiST, whose weights are unavailable) and StableSyncNet [ 3 ] , all run through our pipeline.

paragraphs.en: Per-phone score. A 12 12 -frame ( 480 true ms 480\text{true}\mathrm{ms} ) window slides over the clip with a stride of 1 frame, taking the same 480 true ms 480\text{true}\mathrm{ms} of video and audio at every position. Within each window, forced alignment ( Section 2.2.2 ) gives each phone a video span and an audio span, the tokens its interval covers in each tower. For every phone whose interval is at least 80 true % 80\text{true}\mathrm{\%} covered by the window, the two spans are embedded and their cosine similarity is recorded. paragraphs.en: Benchmark. The per-phone score compares a phone’s video span with its own audio span. To test that it responds to phoneme–viseme agreement, we pair video spans with the audio spans of other phones and ask whether the score separates matching visemes from mismatched ones. We build the benchmark on HDTF [ 22 ] , 805 805 clips of 292 292 speakers, on which no stage of PVSync and none of the baselines was trained. The footage is clean and frontal, the speech well articulated, and each clip’s audio is aligned to its SyncNet-detected offset, so every video span shows the sound of its phone being produced. Phones come from Whisper transcripts force-aligned with MFA and are mapped to the eight viseme classes of Table 5 . The bank holds 2163 2163 phone spans longer than 80 true ms 80\text{true}\mathrm{ms} , 240 to 330 240330 per class and at most seven per clip. Every video span is scored against every audio span from a different speaker, 4.6 4.6 M pairs in all, so the two spans of a pair share nothing but, at most, their viseme class. A pair whose spans share a class is good and should score above the flag threshold. Any other pair is bad and should fall below it. Because the labels come from forced alignment, any transcribed speech dataset yields such a benchmark at any size with no human annotation.

paragraphs.en: Retrieval. For each of the eight viseme classes we average the embeddings of its audio spans into one point, the class centroid, leaving out spans from the clip being queried. A video span is classified correctly at k k when its own viseme class is among the k k centroids closest to it by cosine; retrieval@ k k is this accuracy over all video spans ( Table 4 , last two columns; chance 0.125 0.125 and 0.25 0.25 ). Stage 3 scores 0.74 0.74 at k = 1 k{=}1 and 0.90 0.90 at k = 2 k{=}2 . The audio clusters themselves are well formed, since a nearest-centroid classifier on the audio embeddings alone reaches an accuracy of 0.94 0.94 after stage 3, against 0.70 0.70 after stage 1. The retrieval confusion at k = 1 k{=}1 ( Table 5 ) shows the lip-explicit classes, labiodental (/f, v/) and bilabial (/p, b, m/), retrieved almost perfectly, with the errors falling between classes that look alike on the lips. Open and spread vowels are exchanged, because a vowel such as /æ/ (“cat”) opens the mouth only slightly more than a spread vowel such as /E/ (“bed”). Rhotic and rounded are exchanged, because /r/ is produced with rounded lips. Velar is the weakest class and scatters over its neighbours, because /k/ and /g/ have no lip gesture of their own and the mouth during them shows the neighbouring vowel. paragraphs.en: Generation-model level. Thirteen talking-head video generation models produced 324 324 clips, each shifted to its detected offset so that articulation alone is judged. We asked 180 180 blind raters to score each clip from 1 to 5 on how well the mouth matches the speech. A model’s error rate is the percentage of its phones scored below 0.28 0.28 , a threshold fixed on real footage before the study. Ranked against the raters’ mean scores, the error rate agrees at Spearman 0.83 0.83 , where LSE-C [ 2 ] reaches 0.34 0.34 . By mean rating, five models score above 4 (good), six between 3 and 4 (mid) and two below 3 (bad). The error rate ranks all five good models above every mid and bad model and misorders only two of the twelve mid–bad pairs ( Fig. 1 b).
paragraphs.zh: 生成模型层面。 十三款对话头像视频生成模型共产生了 324 个视频片段，每个片段都根据检测到的偏移量进行了调整，以便仅对口型动作进行评判。 我们邀请 180 名盲测评分员对每个视频片段进行 1 到 5 分的评分，评估其口型与语音的匹配程度。 一个模型的错误率是指其音素中得分低于 0.28 的百分比，这一阈值在研究前已根据真实视频素材确定。 根据评分员的平均得分进行排序，错误率与平均得分的相关性（Spearman 系数）为 0.83，而 LSE-C [2] 的相关性为 0.34。 从平均评分来看，有五款模型的评分高于 4 分（良好），六款在 3 到 4 分之间（中等），两款低于 3 分（较差）。 错误率将五款良好模型全部排在所有中等和较差模型之上，且仅在十二对中等–较差模型中错误排序了两对（图 1b）。

paragraphs.en: Chunk level. We sampled 400 400 chunks of 12 12 frames ( 480 true ms 480\text{true}\mathrm{ms} ) from 240 240 generated talking-head clips held out from all training. Ninety-six blind raters saw each chunk with 13 13 frames of context on either side and offset-corrected audio, and answered yes or no to whether the mouth matches the speech. Each chunk got ten ratings on average, and their majority is its label, 350 350 yes and 50 50 no. Compared with the rest of the panel’s majority, a single rater catches 59 true % 59\text{true}\mathrm{\%} of the chunks the panel flags and wrongly flags 16 true % 16\text{true}\mathrm{\%} of the chunks it accepts. We fix every model’s threshold at this 16 true % 16\text{true}\mathrm{\%} false-flag rate and report the percentage of human-flagged bad chunks it catches, along with its ROC AUC against the majority label ( Table 6 ). We compare our model with the baselines through two scores, the window score of the whole chunk and the worst-phoneme score, the lowest per-phone score ( Section 3.3 ) inside it. The window score reaches an ROC AUC of 0.788 0.788 and catches 56 true % 56\text{true}\mathrm{\%} of the panel’s flags. The worst-phoneme score reaches 0.836 0.836 and catches 70 true % 70\text{true}\mathrm{\%} , above the single rater’s 59 true % 59\text{true}\mathrm{\%} . SyncNet and MTD-VocaLiST trail both of our scores, StableSyncNet ties the window score, and no other model can score a chunk phone by phone.
paragraphs.zh: 片段级别。 我们从所有训练数据中预留的 240 个说话头部剪辑中，采样了 400 个片段，每个片段包含 12 帧（480 true ms 480\text{true}\mathrm{ms}）。 九十六名盲测评分员观看了每个片段，其中每侧包含 13 帧上下文和经过偏移校正的音频，并回答嘴型是否与语音匹配。 每个片段平均获得了十次评分，多数票即为其标签：350 个“是”和 50 个“否”。 与评审团其余成员的多数票相比，单个评分员能正确识别出评审团标记的片段中的 59 true % 59\text{true}\mathrm{\%}，但也会错误标记其接受的片段中的 16 true % 16\text{true}\mathrm{\%}。 我们将每个模型的阈值固定在此 16 true % 16\text{true}\mathrm{\%} 的误报率上，并报告其识别出人标记的不良片段的比例，以及其与多数标签相比的 ROC AUC（表 6）。 我们通过两个分数将我们的模型与基线模型进行比较：整个片段的窗口分数和片段内的最差音素分数（即每个音素的最低分数）（第 3.3 节）。 窗口分数的 ROC AUC 达到了 0.788，并识别出了评审团标记的片段中的 56 true % 56\text{true}\mathrm{\%}。 最差音素分数达到了 0.836，识别率达到了 70 true % 70\text{true}\mathrm{\%}，高于单个评分员的 59 true % 59\text{true}\mathrm{\%}。 SyncNet 和 MTD-VocaLiST 在这两个分数上均落后于我们的模型；StableSyncNet 的窗口分数与之一致，但没有其他模型能够按音素对片段进行评分。

paragraphs.en: The offset-recovery, viseme-mismatch and LRS2 experiments are numerical studies on existing datasets for which no ethical approval was required. The rating studies of Section 3.4 involved paid crowdworkers recruited via Prolific and administered through Mabyduck, who rated the perceptual lip-sync quality of generated videos. Participants were adults (18+) who took part voluntarily after receiving task instructions, and no ethics committee approval was required for this minimal-risk perceptual evaluation task. Participants were compensated at £18.55–£19.67 per hour. The authors received only the ratings, keyed by pseudonymous participant identifiers. Other data comprised publicly available or proprietary research datasets used under their respective licences, and videos generated by the authors using commercial talking-head systems.
